summary.text: For \(n=9\), the first nine primes have product \(223092870\), and the corresponding term factors as \(49770428644836901=29^2\cdot53\cdot1116604864937\). Thus it is not squarefree, so the universal squarefreeness claim—and hence the conjunction—is false.

full_proof.text:
Let \(p_0=2,p_1=3,p_2=5,\ldots\) denote the primes in increasing order, indexed starting at \(0\), and define
\[
P_n=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}p_k,
\qquad
a(n)=P_n^2+1.
\]
(The product is empty when \(n=0\).) The conjecture in question is the conjunction of the following two assertions:

1. \(a(n)\) is squarefree for every nonnegative integer \(n\);
2. the set of indices \(n\) for which \(a(n)\) is prime is infinite.

It suffices to disprove the first assertion, since a conjunction is false as soon as one of its two conjuncts is false.

Consider the index \(n=9\). The first nine primes, with the above zero-based indexing, are
\[
2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23.
\]
Their product is
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_9
 &=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23\\
 &=223092870.
\end{aligned}
\]
For example, this multiplication can be accumulated as
\[
2\cdot3=6,
\quad6\cdot5=30,
\quad30\cdot7=210,
\quad210\cdot11=2310,
\]
\[
2310\cdot13=30030,
\quad30030\cdot17=510510,
\quad510510\cdot19=9699690,
\]
and
\[
9699690\cdot23=223092870.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(9)
  &=223092870^2+1\\
  &=49770428644836901.
\end{aligned}
\]
This integer has the factorization
\[
49770428644836901
 =29^2\cdot59180057841661
 =29^2\cdot53\cdot1116604864937.
\]
Indeed, \(29^2=841\),
\[
53\cdot1116604864937=59180057841661,
\]
and direct multiplication gives
\[
841\cdot59180057841661=49770428644836901.
\]
Thus
\[
29^2\mid a(9).
\]

Recall that a positive integer is squarefree precisely when it is not divisible by the square of any integer greater than \(1\) (equivalently, it is not divisible by the square of any prime). Since \(29>1\), the divisibility \(29^2\mid a(9)\) proves that \(a(9)\) is not squarefree. If one uses the prime-square formulation, note also that \(29\) is prime: a composite divisor would have a prime divisor at most \(\sqrt{29}<6\), but \(29\) is divisible by none of \(2,3,5\).

We have therefore exhibited a specific term of the sequence that is not squarefree:
\[
\boxed{a(9)=49770428644836901\text{ is divisible by }29^2.}
\]
Hence the universal assertion that every \(a(n)\) is squarefree is false. It follows immediately that the combined conjecture
\[
\bigl(\forall n,\ a(n)\text{ is squarefree}\bigr)
\;\land\;
\bigl(\text{infinitely many }a(n)\text{ are prime}\bigr)
\]
is false, irrespective of whether its second, infinitude-of-primes assertion is true or false.
